Project Summary – AstroCare | LOGIC STORM

AstroCare is an application concept designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions by monitoring their physical and mental health. It analyzes important health indicators, identifies unusual changes, and provides alerts and helpful recommendations.

Our project uses NASA data and scientific references to support its concept, while AI tools assisted us in writing and improving the code. Through AstroCare, we aim to make astronaut health monitoring easier and more organized, helping astronauts, space agencies, and researchers identify potential health risks earlier and support safer space missions.
details:
AstroCare – Project Details

1. Project Description

AstroCare is an astronaut health monitoring application designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It monitors important physical and mental health indicators, analyzes health data, identifies unusual changes, and provides alerts and recommendations to help astronauts stay aware of their health conditions.

2. The Problem

Astronauts face several health challenges in space, including microgravity, radiation exposure, sleep disruption, and isolation. These factors may affect their physical and mental health. Monitoring these changes and identifying potential health risks early can be challenging.

3. Our Solution

We developed AstroCare to make astronaut health monitoring easier and more organized. The application analyzes health readings, highlights potential risks, tracks changes, and provides helpful recommendations through a user-friendly interface.

4. How It Works

• Collects astronaut health-related data.
• Analyzes important health indicators.
• Detects unusual changes and potential risks.
• Displays alerts and recommendations.
• Uses simulated scenarios to test the monitoring system.

5. Technologies Used

• Python for backend development and data analysis.
• Artificial Intelligence tools to assist with writing and improving code.
• NASA data and scientific references to support the project.
• Simulation for testing different health scenarios.
• A dashboard to display health information and alerts.

6. Target Audience

• Astronauts.
• Space agencies.
• Space health researchers.
• Future long-duration space missions.

7. Expected Impact

AstroCare aims to support earlier identification of potential health risks, improve health awareness, and organize astronaut health information to support better monitoring during space missions.

8. Future Improvements

• Real-time monitoring using wearable sensors.
• More advanced AI-powered analysis.
• Personalized health recommendations.
• Integration with additional space health datasets.
